Staff Operations Guide

ZooSnooz

The night-time field study, delivered through Taronga Tracka.

Programme
Taronga Zoo Sydney sleepover
Animals
Five, in any order
Per animal
15–20 minutes
Device
One phone per student or pair

01What ZooSnooz is

Students become night researchers. At each of five animals they read a keeper insight, use an on-screen instrument to gather their own data, answer one question about what they found, write an observation, and film a piece to camera. The clips become a documentary they keep.

The app carries the structure, the timing and the marking. Your job is movement, pacing and encouragement, not running the technology.

02The six steps, every animal

STEP 1
Keeper insight
One card. What to watch for.
STEP 2
Instrument
They gather their own data.
STEP 3
One question
About what they just measured.
STEP 4
Observation
Watch, then write.
STEP 5
Film
A short piece to camera.
STEP 6
Badge
Points, then back to the map.

03The map they come back to

The screen a student returns to after every animal, and the one you will be reading over shoulders all night.

  • An animal unlocks on arrival. Until then the card shows how far away it is, so a group can see that they are not there yet.
  • Order does not matter, and walking away costs nothing. A place is held mid-activity, so a group moved on early loses no work.
  • Top right is animals finished out of five. Submit Session ends the night and starts the film.

04The teacher makes an account

Four fields, no invite code, no approval step. They can do it in the car park if they have to, though it is a far better conversation a week out.

  1. Email address. Their school address is fine.
  2. A password, at least six characters, typed twice.
  3. Their school, picked from the list. If it is not there, the + Add option takes it as typed.
  4. An optional tick for Taronga education updates. Nothing depends on it.
The same email and password also sign them into Wildly by Taronga. One login, both products. Forgot password? on the sign-in screen emails a reset, so there is never a code for anyone to chase.

05Then the class

Teacher Dashboard › Create a New Class. Four decisions, and one of them matters more than the others.

  1. Location: pick ZooSnooz. The subject menu disappears when they do, which is correct. ZooSnooz is science, and choosing it is not a decision they have to make.
  2. NSW Stage, 1 to 5. This is the one that matters. It sets the reading level of every prompt and question on the night, and the bar their writing is marked against. A Stage 2 class gets shorter prompts, simpler questions and gentler marking. Get this wrong and a Year 3 meets Year 10 wording in the dark.
  3. Class name. Anything that identifies the group to them later.
  4. Tick the filming consent box. The class will not be created without it. It commits the teacher to obtaining consent from families under their own school’s policy, and the parent letter is linked beside it, ready to print. The same letter stays on the class page afterwards, so it can be reprinted any time.
The class code is generated for them, six characters, once the class is made. That code is the only thing a student needs to join: no account, no email address, no password, no real name.

06What each animal asks for

AnimalInstrumentTimingWhat the student does
Sumatran TigerPanthera tigris sumatrae Energy tracker30 sec Holds a button while the tiger moves and releases when it is still, building an activity timeline.
African LionPanthera leo Sound monitor30 sec Holds the phone towards the enclosure. The microphone tracks volume over time.
Greater One-Horned RhinoRhinoceros unicornis Movement padUntimed Drags a finger across a pad to feel weight and momentum. The app reads the gait: walk, trot or charge.
BinturongArctictis binturong Light scannerUntimed Points the camera around the animal. Reads how well dark fur hides it at that light level.
Sun BearHelarctos malayanus Field sketchUntimed Draws and labels what they can see: the claws, the tongue, the chest patch.
The lion and the tiger are the two on a timer, and both need the group settled and quiet for thirty seconds. Send a restless group to the other three first.

08From the answer to the writing

09How points work

Each animal is worth up to 120 points. The written observation is marked out of 15 across three areas and scaled to 100; a question answered correctly first time adds 20.

AreaWhat earns marksOut of
BehaviourDescribing what the animal is actually doing: moving, resting, hiding, calling5
DetailNaming what they can see: claws, horn, fur, shadow, sounds, surroundings5
WritingLength and clarity, with expectations set by the class stage5
QuestionCorrect on the first attempt20
Marking adjusts to the class stage. A Year 3 answer is held to Year 3 expectations, not the same bar as a Year 11.

ZooSnooz · Staff Operations Guide Filming

10The camera

Each animal ends with a short piece to camera, and a line at the top says what to film. It is optional, and the skip underneath costs no marks.

  • Night lifts a dark enclosure. Worth turning on before they complain the picture is black.
  • Zoom runs 1× to 3×. On a phone with an ultra-wide lens a 0.5× appears as well.
  • Flip swaps between the animal and the student. Most film the animal and talk over it.
  • Recording stops itself. Nobody has to remember to press anything twice.
  • If the picture is a black rectangle, the enclosure is too dark for the phone. Move them closer, turn Night on, and get the white torches off the glass.

11Tell them they are the presenter

This is the single thing that most improves what comes back. A student asked to “record something” mumbles at the glass. A student told they are presenting a wildlife documentary stands up straight and performs. It is their film, with their name on it, and they keep it.

What to say to them

  • “Tell us what you can see, right now.” Present tense, out loud, like someone reporting from where they are standing.
  • “Start with where you are.” I’m here at the Sumatran tigers, and… It gives the clip an opening and it sounds like television.
  • “One thing, not five.” A single detail described properly beats a list every time.

And what to hold them to

  • Ten seconds is plenty. The clip stops itself. Short and certain beats long and mumbled.
  • Quiet voice. It is night, the animals are close, and the microphone is nearer than they think.
  • Not everyone has to be on camera. Anyone who would rather not is the camera operator, and every documentary has one.

ZooSnooz · Staff Operations Guide What they get back

12What they get back

13The documentary

Tapping Submit Session joins their clips into one short film: a title card, a card per animal, their own footage branded over the top, and a closing card. It takes about 45 seconds and is built on the phone itself, not on a server.

Tell students

  • Keep the screen on and the app in front. If the phone locks, the build pauses and waits, so it simply takes longer. Do not reload or close the tab.

What is kept

  • Every clip uploads as it is filmed, so nothing depends on the film succeeding.
  • Raw clips go after 12 months; the film is kept. Teachers see both in their portal.

ZooSnooz · Staff Operations Guide Running the night

14The running order

  1. Start at the Institute or the Food Market. Both have wifi. Get every phone onto it before anyone walks off, because each clip uploads as it is filmed.
  2. Join the class. The teacher gives out the class code and each student picks an animal alias. No real names are ever entered.
  3. Check the phones. Charged, auto-lock off or on its longest setting.
  4. Hand out the red torches, and say what they are for. Red preserves night vision, disturbs the animals far less, and is the difference between usable footage and a black rectangle. White torches on the glass ruin both.
  5. Split the group. Not everyone at the same animal. Send a restless group to the rhino, binturong or sun bear first, because those three are untimed.
  6. Work the five animals, in any order. Fifteen to twenty minutes each. The lion and tiger need quiet and stillness for thirty seconds. A student who arrives late has lost nothing: their place is held.
  7. Bring everyone back to the Institute or the Food Market. Same two spots, same reason. The film is built on the phone, but the clips and the finished film still have to upload, and that is where the signal is.
  8. Submit Session, together. About 45 seconds each. Screens stay on and the app stays in front while it builds. This is the moment worth standing over.

15Worth knowing

  • No student ever enters a real name. They are a Quoll or a Bilby all night.
  • Filming is opt-out, arranged by the school. A student who is not being filmed operates the camera for their group.
  • Nothing a student does can delete another student’s work.

16After the night

Nothing is left for anyone to collect. It is already where the teacher needs it.

  • Every clip, every film and every piece of writing is on the class page, filed under the student’s alias. The teacher plays them there, and can download them.
  • The marking is already done. Each animal carries its three sub-scores and its points, so a teacher reads results rather than marks a set.
  • Taronga staff can pull any film from the staff portal if a school loses theirs or asks for a copy later.

ZooSnooz · Staff Operations Guide When something goes wrong

17If something goes wrong

None of these loses a student’s work. Say that out loud first, because it is the thing they are actually worried about.

The film has the cards but none of the footage

The screen will say why. If it mentions opening in Safari, do that. Some browsers will not let the app read video back. Every clip is already saved either way, so nothing is lost, and the film can be rebuilt afterwards.

The camera will not start

The browser is blocking it. Reload the page and allow camera access when asked. If it still refuses, they can skip the film and keep going. It costs no marks.

The microphone is unavailable on the lion

Tap continue and watch quietly instead. It does not block progress or cost marks.

A student has lost their place, or swapped phones

Their work is saved against their alias. Rejoining with the same class code and the same alias restores it. If the app will not let them back in on a different handset, the teacher can release the record from the class portal.

There is no reception at the enclosure

Everything works except uploading, and the clips catch up when signal returns. Keep walking.

The phone is nearly flat

Finish the animal they are on and Submit Session before the battery goes. The film is built on the phone, so it needs enough charge for about a minute of work.

The class code is not recognised

Codes are six characters and are not case sensitive. Check it against the teacher’s own screen rather than a handwritten copy. 0 and O are the usual culprits.
